date_note: The Epoch Times (21 Nov) says Trump selected Davies on Thursday, 19 November; the White House release was not read.
exec: Leadership change at the US office that coordinates national cyber policy; may affect federal cyber priorities and planned programs.
org: Office of the National Cyber Director
plain: The US national cyber director, Sean Cairncross, is out, and the Pentagon's chief information officer, Kirsten Davies, has been named to the job. The White House has not said whether she is acting or nominated.
summary: SecurityWeek reports Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies has been appointed National Cyber Director, replacing Sean Cairncross. The Epoch Times says Trump selected her on Thursday and the White House did not confirm whether she is acting director or a nominee. It says Cairncross was fired and quotes Trump: "Because I didn't think that person was good enough." Nextgov, citing Axios, first reported the change.
title: Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies named US national cyber director as Sean Cairncross leaves

validation.note: SecurityWeek and The Epoch Times (both 21 Nov, read 22 Nov) each state the appointment; The Epoch Times quotes Trump on the firing; the whitehouse.gov release SecurityWeek links was not read. Earlier: Nextgov/FCW (cites Axios) and CyberScoop (anonymous source close to the White House, no Axios citation) read. Anadolu (Nov 20) says a White House official confirmed the departure and that Secretary of State Rubio congratulated Davies as new director on X; Gizmodo calls her acting director and says the reason was not officially stated. Reasons for departure differ in coverage and are not stated here as fact.
